variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start in A: move to the top of the visible button to prepare. Select A whenever the hand is not yet in the prepared position. The prepared pose in these observations has the wrist above the button, height approximately 0.15, and closed fingers; do not mistake the wrist's image position for the fingertips' contact point. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. If passage_count equals N-1 and the next target passage is approximately 35 or fewer time units away, select C. Estimate the upcoming arrival from the chronological cube motion shown at this step, accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. A useful estimate fits smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to the current interval's timestamped cube positions and finds its next crossing of the visible target x; do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant. In particular, an endpoint turnaround can already be the press-launch time for a fast cube. The final shown decisions in episodes 23 and 32 are such turnarounds; those in episodes 66, 94, and 99 show motion toward the requested next passage. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. If motion timing is uncertain, default to B while refining the estimate from the next observations, rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

fields.name: passage_count
fields.description: Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, including the final decision observation after the preceding execution observations, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side (0 for empty memory). Compute the sign of cube x minus target x: strictly negative is -1 and strictly positive is 1, however small the separation. Do not introduce a proximity deadband or require a later confirmation frame. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. A change first visible in the final decision observation counts immediately. If the preceding side is 0, the first nonzero sign establishes the side without incrementing. At exact equality retain the working side and do not increment. Compute passage_count and last_side from this same scan and write both resulting values together. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: The number of completed target-center passages by the cube up to and including this decision's final observation. Count passages in both directions, including during preparation; do not count proximity alone. A passage occurs when cube x minus target x changes sign along the continuous motion. Initialize to 0. The values by decision step are: episode 23: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 32: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 66: 0,0,1,1; episode 94: 0,0,1,2,2; episode 99: 0,0,1,1. e.g. 2

fields.name: last_side
fields.description: Write the working side resulting from the same chronological scan used for passage_count, after processing every newly shown observation including the final decision frame. Set it to -1 when cube x is strictly smaller than target x and 1 when it is strictly larger, even when the separation is small. Retain the preceding nonzero side only at exact equality; use 0 only if no nonzero side has yet been observed. Do not require a confirmation frame or wait for the cube to move clear of the target. Record this observed side, not the side expected after the selected command. e.g. -1
fields.annotation: The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1

history.critique:
field passage_count, POLICY PROMPT
  When the goal requested the fourth arrival, the incoming count was 2 and the cube was last on the smaller-x side. The newly shown motion ended just beyond the target center on the larger-x side, so the outgoing annotated count was 3. The policy instead retained 2. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in applying the update to the final observation, not a need for additional history. Explicitly require processing the final decision observation as well as all preceding execution observations before writing memory. A small but strictly positive cube-x-minus-target-x value is positive: do not introduce a proximity deadband, require a later confirmation frame, or postpone counting until the cube has moved well clear of the target. Increment on each observed change between nonzero sides, including a change first visible in the final frame. Exact equality alone retains the preceding side and does not increment. Write the completed count, for example 3, without counting the command about to be selected.

field last_side, POLICY PROMPT
  In the same fourth-arrival situation, the final observation placed the cube just beyond the target center, but the policy retained the incoming smaller-x side instead of the annotated larger-x side. This breaks PREDICTABILITY by omitting the final observation from the effective update. Explicitly state that last_side must be the working side after processing every shown observation, including the final decision frame. Set it to -1 for a strictly smaller cube x and 1 for a strictly larger cube x, even when the separation is small; retain the previous nonzero side only at exact equality. Initialize to 0 only when no nonzero side has yet been observed. In this situation the outgoing example value is 1. Compute this field and passage_count from the same chronological scan so that a newly counted passage and its new side are written together.
